title: Sharps Injury Log
about: The log OSHA requires of employers who keep an injury and illness log under 29 CFR 1904: each needlestick or cut from a contaminated sharp, kept so the injured worker cannot be identified, for 5 years. Offices of physicians, outpatient care centers and medical labs are partly exempt from Part 1904 and from this log, but OSHA encourages them to keep it. Some state plans (California, 8 CCR 5193) ask for more; the extra columns are for them.

source.name: OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens, 29 CFR 1910.1030(h)(5), and 29 CFR 1904.33 (eCFR, 2026-10-20)

blocks.text: Write each injury from a contaminated sharp here, as soon as it is reported. Do not write the injured worker's name: use the case number from their confidential exposure report, so no one can tell who was hurt from this log.

blocks.label: More detail, where a state plan asks for it
columns: Safety feature on the device, and was it activated

blocks.text: Keep this log for 5 years after the end of the calendar year it covers. If the type or brand of a device cannot be found out without risking another exposure, write unknown.
